items.q: By the end of this decade, the orbiting telescope ______ data for longer than any of its predecessors.
items.vi: Đến cuối thập kỷ này, kính viễn vọng trên quỹ đạo sẽ đã thu thập dữ liệu lâu hơn bất kỳ kính tiền nhiệm nào.
items.explanation: By the end of this decade sets a future deadline and for longer than stresses duration up to it, so the future perfect continuous will have been collecting is required. ✗ will collect — simple future cannot show duration up to a deadline; ✗ is collecting — present continuous describes now, not a future point; ✗ has been collecting — present perfect measures duration up to now, not up to a future date.

items.q: The minister spent ten minutes ______ before finally admitting that the excavation had been cancelled.
items.vi: Bà bộ trưởng vòng vo mất mười phút rồi cuối cùng mới thừa nhận rằng cuộc khai quật đã bị hủy.
items.explanation: Beat around the bush = avoid saying something directly, which matches before finally admitting after ten minutes of talk. ✗ barking up the wrong tree — pursuing a mistaken idea, not delaying an admission; ✗ jumping the gun — acting too soon, the opposite of stalling; ✗ burning her bridges — destroying any way back, unrelated to avoiding a topic.

items.q: Insurers were reluctant to ______ the deep-sea expedition, since nobody could put a price on the risk of losing the submersible.
items.vi: Các hãng bảo hiểm ngần ngại bảo lãnh cho chuyến thám hiểm biển sâu, vì không ai định giá nổi rủi ro mất chiếc tàu lặn.
items.explanation: Underwrite = accept financial responsibility for a risk, which is what insurers do and why the risk of losing the submersible makes them reluctant. ✗ undercut — sell cheaper than a rival, not insure; ✗ outbid — offer more money than others at a sale; ✗ overcharge — ask too high a price, and insurers here are not selling.

items.q: The launch has been ______ to October after engineers found a hairline crack in a fuel line.
items.vi: Vụ phóng đã bị lùi sang tháng Mười sau khi các kỹ sư phát hiện một vết nứt li ti trên đường ống nhiên liệu.
items.explanation: Push back = postpone to a later date, so to October after engineers found a crack means the launch was delayed. ✗ pushed for — campaign for something, not move a date; ✗ pulled back — withdraw or retreat, does not take a new date; ✗ pushed on — continue despite difficulty, the opposite of a delay.

items.q: The eroding cliff poses a ______ threat to the Roman fort perched on top of it.
items.vi: Vách đá đang xói mòn là một mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng đối với pháo đài La Mã nằm chênh vênh bên trên.
items.explanation: Grave threat (like serious threat) is the fixed collocation for a threat that could cause great harm, fitting an eroding cliff under a fort. ✗ heavy — collocates with rain, traffic or losses, not threat; ✗ high — goes with risk or price, but we do not say 'a high threat to'; ✗ deep — goes with concern or trouble, never with threat.

items.q: The safety board recommended that the airline ______ every aircraft of that type until the fault was traced.
items.vi: Ủy ban an toàn khuyến nghị rằng hãng hàng không đình bay mọi máy bay loại đó cho tới khi tìm ra lỗi.
items.explanation: After recommended that, the verb is in the subjunctive base form ground, whatever the subject or the tense of the main verb. ✗ grounds — third-person -s is dropped in the subjunctive; ✗ grounded — the past tense of 'recommended' is not copied into the that-clause; ✗ would ground — 'would' is not used after recommend that (only 'should' or the base form).

items.q: Cruise lines expect to ______ the cost of the new terminals within a decade through higher berthing fees.
items.vi: Các hãng du thuyền dự kiến thu hồi chi phí xây các bến cảng mới trong vòng một thập kỷ nhờ phí neo đậu cao hơn.
items.explanation: Recoup = get back money you have spent, so the cruise lines recover the cost of the new terminals themselves. ✗ refund — give money back to a customer, paying out not taking in; ✗ reimburse — pay someone back for their expenses, again money going out; ✗ redeem — exchange a voucher or pay off a debt, not recover a cost.

items.q: The hotel staff ______ to make the stranded passengers comfortable, even lending out their own phone chargers.
items.vi: Nhân viên khách sạn đã hết lòng hết sức để hành khách bị mắc kẹt được thoải mái, thậm chí cho mượn cả sạc điện thoại của mình.
items.explanation: Bend over backwards = try extremely hard to help, and even lending out their own chargers shows that effort. ✗ turned over a new leaf — started behaving better, not helping others; ✗ got cold feet — lost their nerve, which does not fit making guests comfortable; ✗ let their hair down — relaxed and had fun, not worked hard for passengers.

items.q: These bones ______ to a child; the growth plates had already fused when the person died.
items.vi: Những mẩu xương này không thể là của một đứa trẻ; các đĩa sụn tăng trưởng đã liền hẳn khi người đó qua đời.
items.explanation: The fused growth plates are evidence, so this is a confident deduction that something was impossible: can't have + past participle. ✗ mustn't have belonged — 'must have' is used only for positive deduction; its negative is 'can't have'; ✗ needn't have belonged — means it was unnecessary, not impossible; ✗ shouldn't have belonged — means it was wrong to, a judgement not a deduction.

items.q: The museum ______ several retired teachers ______ leading the weekend tours when its own guides fell ill.
items.vi: Bảo tàng đã lôi kéo mấy giáo viên về hưu vào việc dẫn các tour cuối tuần khi hướng dẫn viên của họ ngã bệnh.
items.explanation: Rope someone into doing something = persuade them to take on a task they had not planned, and the -ing form leading confirms the preposition into. ✗ tied / into — tie into = connect one thing to another, not persuade; ✗ roped / on — rope takes 'in' or 'into', never 'on'; ✗ hauled / in — haul in = drag or arrest, and 'in' cannot precede 'leading'.

items.q: Not until the ice cores had been analysed ______ how abruptly the climate had shifted.
items.vi: Mãi đến khi các lõi băng được phân tích, các nhà khoa học mới nhận ra khí hậu đã thay đổi đột ngột đến mức nào.
items.explanation: A sentence opening with Not until… inverts the main clause: auxiliary + subject + base verb, so did scientists realise. ✗ scientists realised — no inversion after a fronted negative; ✗ had scientists realised — the realising came after the analysis, so past perfect puts it at the wrong, earlier time; ✗ scientists did realise — the auxiliary must come before the subject.

items.q: The council will ______ a small charge on every hotel night to pay for repairs to the medieval walls.
items.vi: Hội đồng thành phố sẽ áp một khoản phí nhỏ lên mỗi đêm lưu trú khách sạn để trả cho việc sửa chữa tường thành thời trung cổ.
items.explanation: You impose a tax, charge or fine on people, so a small charge on every hotel night is imposed. ✗ inflict — goes with pain, damage or a defeat, not a fee; ✗ exert — goes with pressure, influence or force; ✗ instil — put values or feelings into someone, never a charge.

items.q: ______ from the same volcanic rock as the temple, the statues have weathered surprisingly little.
items.vi: Được tạc từ cùng loại đá núi lửa với ngôi đền, các bức tượng phong hóa ít đến ngạc nhiên.
items.explanation: The statues were carved by someone, so the reduced clause needs the past participle Carved with passive meaning. ✗ Carving — active, would make the statues the ones doing the carving; ✗ Having carved — active perfect, same wrong doer; ✗ To carve — an infinitive of purpose, which says nothing about where the statues came from.

items.q: The probe's landing sequence worked, but engineers admitted it had survived the descent ______.
options: by the skin of its teeth
items.answer: by the skin of its teeth
items.vi: Chuỗi thao tác hạ cánh của tàu thăm dò đã thành công, nhưng các kỹ sư thừa nhận nó đã sống sót qua pha hạ cánh trong gang tấc.
items.explanation: By the skin of its teeth = only just, narrowly, fitting worked, but … admitted — success that was nearly failure. ✗ by leaps and bounds — very quickly, used of progress; ✗ by word of mouth — through people telling each other; ✗ by the book — strictly following the rules, which says nothing about a narrow escape.

items.q: Pollen trapped in the lake bed has ______ new light on how the harbour silted up.
items.vi: Phấn hoa mắc kẹt dưới đáy hồ đã soi rọi thêm về cách cảng biển bị bồi lấp.
items.explanation: Shed light on (also throw or cast light on) = help explain something, and how the harbour silted up is the mystery explained. ✗ given — a lamp gives light literally, but 'give light on' is not an idiom; ✗ put — 'put light on' does not exist; ✗ set — 'set light to' means ignite, and takes 'to' not 'on'.

items.q: ______ carefully a mission is planned, the launch still depends on the weather on the day.
items.vi: Dù một sứ mệnh được lên kế hoạch kỹ lưỡng đến đâu, vụ phóng vẫn phụ thuộc vào thời tiết trong ngày.
items.explanation: No matter how + adverb + clause = however carefully, and the adverb carefully right after the blank decides it. ✗ Even though — must be followed by a subject, not an adverb; ✗ Whatever — takes a noun (whatever the plan); ✗ Despite — a preposition needing a noun or -ing form, not a clause.

items.q: The bronze helmet ______ a record price at auction, three times the estimate printed in the catalogue.
items.vi: Chiếc mũ trụ bằng đồng đã được bán với giá kỷ lục tại phiên đấu giá, gấp ba lần mức ước tính in trong catalogue.
items.explanation: An object fetches a price = is sold for that amount, so the helmet … a record price at auction is the clue. ✗ charged — a seller charges a buyer; a helmet cannot; ✗ spent — a person spends money; an object does not; ✗ afforded — afford = have enough money to buy, again only for people.

items.q: Having lived at the desert camp for months, the team had grown used ______ without running water.
items.vi: Sau nhiều tháng sống ở trại giữa sa mạc, cả đội đã quen với việc không có nước máy.
items.explanation: In grow used to, 'to' is a preposition, so it takes the -ing form: used to living. ✗ to live — 'used to + base verb' means a past habit (formerly lived) and does not follow 'grow'; ✗ living — the 'to' after 'used' is missing; ✗ live — a bare verb cannot follow 'used'.

items.q: The guide ______ the tangled history of the temple so clearly that even the youngest visitors could follow it.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên trình bày lịch sử rối rắm của ngôi đền rõ ràng đến mức ngay cả những du khách nhỏ tuổi nhất cũng theo dõi được.
items.explanation: Put across = communicate an idea so people understand it, and so clearly that … could follow it confirms this. ✗ put off — postpone or discourage; ✗ put down — criticise someone or write something down; ✗ put up — build something or give someone a bed.

items.q: The tools, only half of ______ have been catalogued so far, date from the early Bronze Age.
items.vi: Những công cụ này, mà mới chỉ một nửa được lập danh mục, có niên đại từ đầu thời đại đồ đồng.
items.explanation: Quantifier + of which starts a non-defining relative clause about things, and the tools are things. ✗ them — a pronoun cannot join two clauses with only a comma; it would need 'and'; ✗ whom — used for people; ✗ whose — shows possession and is followed by a noun, so it cannot come after 'of'.

items.q: With the conference paper due on Monday, the two researchers ______ all weekend.
items.vi: Bài báo hội nghị phải nộp vào thứ Hai nên hai nhà nghiên cứu đã thức trắng làm việc suốt cả cuối tuần.
items.explanation: Burn the midnight oil = work late into the night, fitting paper due on Monday and all weekend. ✗ hit the sack — go to bed, the opposite of working late; ✗ threw in the towel — gave up, which does not fit meeting a deadline; ✗ got the sack — were dismissed from a job.

items.q: Entrance fees help to ______ the cost of conserving the mosaics, but they never cover it entirely.
items.vi: Tiền vé vào cửa giúp bù đắp một phần chi phí bảo tồn các bức tranh khảm, nhưng không bao giờ trang trải được toàn bộ.
items.explanation: Defray a cost = provide money to pay part or all of it, matching help to … but never cover it entirely. ✗ deduct — subtract an amount from a total, not pay a cost; ✗ deplete — use up a supply, which fees do not do to a cost; ✗ default — fail to pay a debt, and it takes 'on', not an object.

items.q: The tourism board now wishes it ______ its marketing budget just before the pandemic struck.
items.vi: Giờ đây cơ quan du lịch ước gì họ đã không cắt ngân sách quảng bá ngay trước khi đại dịch ập đến.
items.explanation: A regret about a past action after wish takes the past perfect, and just before the pandemic struck puts the cut in the past: hadn't cut. ✗ didn't cut — past simple after wish is a wish about the present; ✗ wouldn't cut — wish + would complains about someone's future or repeated behaviour; ✗ hasn't cut — the present perfect is never used after wish.

items.q: Restoring the mosaic ______ the city an arm and a ______, but visitor numbers have doubled since it reopened.
items.vi: Việc phục chế bức tranh khảm khiến thành phố tốn một khoản tiền khổng lồ, nhưng lượng khách tham quan đã tăng gấp đôi từ khi mở cửa lại.
items.explanation: The idiom is cost (someone) an arm and a leg = be extremely expensive; both verb and final noun are fixed. ✗ paid / foot — the restoration does not pay anything, and 'an arm and a foot' is not the idiom; ✗ charged / hand — charge takes a price, and 'hand' breaks the phrase; ✗ spent / leg — spending is done by the city, not by 'restoring the mosaic'.

items.q: The authorities have ______ the ban on photography inside the tomb, to the delight of tour groups.
items.vi: Nhà chức trách đã dỡ bỏ lệnh cấm chụp ảnh bên trong lăng mộ, khiến các đoàn du khách vui mừng.
items.explanation: You lift a ban, restriction or sanction = end it, and to the delight of tour groups shows the ban was removed. ✗ raised — raise means move higher or increase, so a raised ban would be stricter, not gone; ✗ risen — intransitive, cannot take the object 'the ban'; ✗ elevated — move to a higher position or rank, not end.
